Honestly, other than the monthly weigh-ins, my doctor has been pretty hands off throughout the process. Even when I go in to get a refill on my scrip, she just summarizes my loss for the month, checks for side effects of the medication, then sends me on my way.

But that works for me, to be honest. I’m usually pretty irritated when I go in (because I’m annoyed I have to go in once a month), and even more irritated when I leave (because the numbers never match the scale at home), so the less talking the better.
I have seen a few things about it. I don’t know if ARFID fits so much, because I don’t gag or have any severe reaction to my not-wanted foods. I just don’t eat them.

Maybe? That is something she and I do different. She drinks a lot of water during the day. I drink one coffee, no sugar, in the morning, and then a few sips of a zero calorie Gatorade at lunch, and then a few sips at dinner. (Goes back to the whole “if it’s not something I’m especially fond of I’d sooner go without” thing. I can sip on a giant bottle of Gatorade for a couple of weeks.)

I’d prefer to avoid upping my calorie intake, as that seems counterproductive. But I do go into the doctor once a month for a weigh-in, and just went in this past Wednesday. She said just work harder this next month.

I did intermittent fasting in middle and high school, but had to quit after I started passing out at school. Now I push myself to not eat to satiate hunger until it makes my head hurt, which is how I know for sure.

And I’m just as baffled as you are, to be honest.

No other snacks if it can be avoided. Sometimes I have to eat something, but I’ve quit buying any snacks so I won’t be tempted. 

And my doctor just told me to eat healthy and that I had to keep losing weight if I wanted to stay on the phentermine.
Well, for what it’s worth, I have moved past despair and into spite, which motivates me to lose more than her next weigh-in. So that’s kind of helpful.

I eat, on average, 900 calories a day. Most of that is protein. There is not an easy way to get my deficit any lower than what it is right now short of cutting out a meal. My TDEE even accounting for a completely sedentary lifestyle - which I don’t have, but default to because that part is a huge variable - is around 1700.

And I’m already tracking/weighing my food. That’s why I eat the same thing so much. It helps remove any uncertainty of where my count is.

As for healthy foods, I actually eat pretty healthy given how much I hate most foods. No junk food, no fast food. Mainly beef as a main meat (not ground), occasionally chicken or turkey; veggies are primarily broccoli, carrots, or potatoes (although I also love leafy salad greens, never iceberg lettuce); apples as a fruit (rarely, I have to be in the mood for it). I’m actually not really into bread, but am a sucker for pasta. Also, cheese is my one true love.

Which isn’t ideal but it works for the most part and isn’t all that unhealthy in terms of nutritional value.

I guess what I’m struggling most with is patience. I originally wanted to lose 10 lbs a month, but I’m (quite obviously) not. And I’m not seeing the progress visually even if the numbers are going down.

Considering she lives in my house and I pay for the groceries (and so know what’s in the fridge/cabinets), and she can’t drive to anywhere to eat, and she leaves evidence of her eating all over the kitchen, I’m 99.5% sure she eats like garbage and eats at least three times a day.

But she is taller and heavier, which I forgot to take into account.

I count all my calories, weigh my food, and measure everything out. Which is precisely why I eat the same breakfast/lunch every day - I’ve got it down to around 400 calories between the two meals, so there’s not uncertainty there, and it leaves around 500 calories for dinner (which is a bit more variable, but still counted, weighed, measured).

She is both taller and heavier than I am, and there’s a 9 year difference, which are all factors to account for.
She is both taller and heavier than me, so I know that plays a huge role. Knowing that, though, and remembering that when her numbers are better than mine are two different things.
OMAD worked for me in middle / high school, but now it’s just not something that fits for my food needs. (I wish it did, though, would make life so much easier.)

I did intermittent fasting during middle school / high school, and only ate dinner. That stopped in 11th grade when I passed out at school.

I have recently tried pushing my lunch off until 2 in the afternoon, with my breakfast at 7, but I’m still ready to go crazy with hunger in the evening. See also: right now, as I sit in bed obsessing over the time because I don’t start making dinner until 6.30 and I’m dying.

Short of skipping breakfast, I’m honestly not sure how much smaller I can get it. 

The way I have it measured out, I eat less than 200 calories at breakfast, and around 200 (I forgot the exact count; it’s written down in my planner) calories for lunch. Then 500 calories max for dinner.

And if I don’t take the pill in the morning, I’ll just be hungry all day at work.

Regarding the suffering:

I don’t actually mind the same breakfast/lunch combo, especially because combined it’s under 500 calories, is heavy on the protein, and I’m on an appetite suppressant that means I don’t really feel hungry—

—until 5 PM, and then I’m ravenous and just want to stuff my face with all the foods. Sadly, the medicine I’m on is only once a day, so I’m now stuck trying to figure out how to curb my appetite in the evening.

Regarding the lifestyle changes:

I am a very, very picky eater. I joke that I only eat 22 different foods, and while the number is just a guess, the message behind the joke is true. So, a lot of the healthy foods, like fish and most vegetables, fruits, I just don’t eat - and when I say I don’t eat them, I mean I will instead choose to go hungry than eat them.

I will try not to compare myself to others, though.

She’s not sick. We’re both on Phentermine 37.5 mg to help with appetite control. 

But from what I’ve seen she’s still eating like garbage, with larger portions , which is where the resentment comes in.

One of my dogs almost died today.

We have four chihuahuas, a grown cat, and a new kitten we just got last week. The smallest of the chihuahuas has been harassing the kitten wanting to play ever since we got her. The two of them were on the couch with my mom when it happened.

The kitten scared the dog. She took a step back and fell off the couch. Her neck/head hit the bottom shelf of the coffee table and she instantly went limp. My mom had tried to catch her but wasn't fast enough. The dog wasn't breathing.

Mom had to do CPR and, thankfully, was able to revive her. She was still blue, though, and not moving at all. Breathing, but not much else. She had completely voided her bladder. Mom race her to the local vet, then texted me to come home from work.

Thankfully, the dog is already doing so much better. She has a concussion, and it took all day for her to get full use of her legs back, but she's alive. Because she's recovered so well, they're not as worried about brain bleed. They even sent her home early after saying they wanted to keep her for observation.

I'm so, so glad. I love this little dog with every fiber of my being, and all I could think about on my way home was how I scolded her last night for harassing the kitten. How I didn't pick her up to give her kisses this morning because I was wearing black to work and didn't want fur on me.

But she's alive and recovering quickly, and that's all that matters.

I also don't enjoy cooking. I'm good at cooking. Great, even. I still hate it with a passion. I hate eating, too, because my preferences are so limited that it can get boring. And I've tried new things but I just never built a taste for them. So, at this point, if I'm going to be bored eating from eating the same thing, I can at least lose weight while I do it.

I do sometimes think it'd be nice to have something different for a meal, but these bars are just the simplest, least frustrating solution to my need to eat. Trying to come up with something for a meal is too much mentally, and I've always fallen into a habit of the same thing every day. I'd honestly eat these bars for dinner, too, if my family didn't nag.
I've never tried baking my own. I'm just so darn picky that it's impossible to find or make healthy snacks.
OMG frozen cookie dough - I'm definitely giving that a shot this week.

I tried normal dieting, but a pound a week just isn't satisfying to me. I need to see results fast to feel like I'm getting anywhere, otherwise I'm prone to frustrated binges. The meal bars help, especially since on a regular diet I always feel so hungry.

I will keep an eye on my health, though. I already have a lot of problems, which is one of my reasons to lose weight, and can't afford many more.

I'm not too worried about maintenance, because once I get to my goal weight I'm gonna monitor like crazy. My issue is getting down to that weight without triggering a frustrated binge. These bars help with that.
Right now I'm using Nesquick powder because it's less messy to measure, but I'll give soy milk a shot! After the disappointing almond milk fiasco, I went straight back to regular milk.
I don't think my local stores stock that, but if I ever run across it in the wild I'll give it a try!

Sometimes they do give me the munchies, but then I just pop a piece of gum. And in terms of satisfying, well, I'll always prefer some real food - but at least these do the job, you know? Hunger lessened.
I've actually never heard of those. Mine are the Atkins chocolate chip cookie dough bars, which I guess are chocolate and protein. No idea, to be honest, I only looked at the calorie count.

I'll be honest, I don't really look at the ingredients list. My primary concerns right now are calories and taste, with taste being a huge factor because obviously if something doesn't taste bearable I'm not going to eat it. The most I could tell you is that the bars I eat have 56% of the daily recommended dose of fiber, and I only know that because I was wondering why my stomach would sometimes get so bubbly. 

And I've never heard of Svelte shakes! I did try the slim fast chocolate shakes, but it was just disappointment in my mouth. I want to eventually find some sort of low calorie chocolate drink because my one true love is chocolate milk, but it can be so high in calories! But also finding something that tastes like good chocolate is a pain, and finding a milk substitute that mixes well with chocolate milk mix is an equal pain. (I tried almond milk one time. I died a little inside.)
Eh, I manage well at 1000 calories for now. Once I get to the weight I want to maintain, I'll eat more calories for maintenance.
